title: Rafael and the Oath
premise: Gideon Almeida, a bone-carver who hears the dead in a valley where magic cannot follow, is bound by an oath to his late mother to never leave. When a dying stranger presses a map into his hands and dies whispering Gideon's true name, he learns the stranger sold his own soul to the court beneath the mountain—and that Gideon's mother made a similar bargain to keep him safe. Joined by Sefa, a disgraced oath-keeper, and Wren, a child who remembers being a fox, Gideon journeys to the subterranean court to steal back three souls before the thirteenth moon turns. He succeeds only by breaking his oath of invisibility, offering his silence—the gift of hearing the dead—as payment, and discovers that love freely chosen outweighs any duty sworn in fear.
about_author: Lena Okonkwo is a former archivist who grew up between Lagos and Lisbon, collecting funeral songs from both cultures. She writes fantasy about grief, bargains, and the families we build when blood fails us.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the magic-dead valley, Gideon carves bones for the grieving and secretly listens to the dead they hold. His mother's deathbed oath—never leave—has kept him safe for ten years. When a wounded stranger stumbles into his workshop speaking Gideon's childhood name, the valley's protective numbness cracks for the first time. Beat: uneasy comfort shattered.

chapters.title: A Map Pressed Into Unwilling Hands
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The stranger, Corvin, dies at dawn, pressing a bone map into Gideon's hands and confessing he sold his soul to the court beneath the mountain. The dead man's voice lingers, begging. Gideon tries to burn the map; it will not burn. The valley elders sense the intrusion and grow watchful. Beat: guilt and the first pull toward duty beyond himself.

chapters.title: What the Oath Was Really For
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa, an oath-keeper exiled for exposing a corrupt vow, arrives hunting Corvin's debt and finds Gideon instead. She reveals the truth: Gideon's mother sold her own voice to the court to buy her son's invisibility—and the thirteenth moon will claim all unpaid souls, hers included. Beat: devastating revelation reframing everything Gideon believed.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With four moons remaining, Gideon breaks his oath and crosses the valley's edge, where magic floods back into him painfully—he can now hear the living too, every want and fear. Sefa guides him toward the mountain; the map pulls like a compass of bone. Beat: terror and exhilaration of a world finally real.

chapters.title: The Child Who Was a Fox
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a border town, the pair are robbed by a pickpocket who turns out to be Wren, a child transformed by the court as payment for her parents' debts, half-remembering fur and forest. Gideon hears the fox-soul still singing inside her. Against Sefa's counsel, he promises to steal her soul back too. Beat: found family begins, chosen over caution.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Pursued by the court's tithe-collectors, the trio shelters with a village that survives by feeding travelers to the mountain. Sefa considers trading Gideon to save herself; Wren's trust shames her into warning him instead. They escape through the tithe-tunnels using Corvin's map. Beat: loyalty tested and quietly chosen.

chapters.title: Doors Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The map leads them to the court's gate, which opens only to a soul willingly offered. Gideon nearly sacrifices himself, but Wren reveals the gate also opens to a soul freely given back—a loophole Corvin died trying to use. They enter posing as a debt-payment. Beat: dread sharpened by fragile hope.

chapters.title: The Court of Counted Souls
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the candlelit court, souls hang like lanterns, each labeled with its price. Gideon finds his mother's voice-soul and Corvin's, but the Queen of Ledgers offers a bargain: leave with two, abandon one. Gideon refuses to choose, buying time by carving the Queen a portrait in bone—an art she has never been shown. Beat: awe curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. As the moon completes its turn, the ledger comes due. Gideon offers his silence—the hearing of the dead—to erase all three debts, breaking his mother's bargain and his own invisibility forever. The Queen accepts; the souls fly free. Gideon goes deaf to the dead but, for the first time, fully present to the living. Beat: climax through sacrifice, not violence.

chapters.title: Carving New Bones
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The trio returns to the valley, which no longer numbs Gideon but no longer imprisons him either. He reopens his workshop with Sefa and Wren beside him, carving memorials he cannot hear but can honor. His mother's freed voice visits once, wordless and warm, before moving on. Beat: quiet resolution—love chosen over oaths, family made, not owed.
